camelback-echo-canyon.note: Echo Canyon Trail is open today under normal hours. The City of Phoenix confirmed a mandatory Trail Heat Safety Program closure of 8am to 5pm daily for Echo Canyon, Cholla, and Piestewa Peak Summit Trail from Monday, August 17 through Thursday, August 20, 2026. The Extreme Heat Watch for the Phoenix metro area has been upgraded to an Extreme Heat Warning, effective August 17, 10am, through August 21, 8pm MST, for afternoon highs of 108 to 112 degrees; no warning is active yet as of today's check. Separately, Echo Canyon Trail is now scheduled to close entirely September 2 through 18, 2026 for its own construction project, following the Cholla Trail sewer diversion closure of August 17 through 28, 2026; expect reduced full-mountain Camelback access for much of the period from August 17 through September 18. Hike before 8am or after 7pm and carry extra water on open hours. Source: City of Phoenix Parks and Recreation; National Weather Service; azfamily.com.

camelback-cholla.note: Cholla Trail closes entirely August 17 through 28, 2026 for the Cholla Sewer Diversion and Abandonment Project; confirmed unchanged as of today. Source: City of Phoenix Water Services Department; City of Phoenix Parks and Recreation; National Weather Service; azfamily.com.

No Extreme Heat Warning was active for the Grand Canyon area below 4000 feet as of the same check. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park; National Weather Service Flagstaff.

north-kaibab-coconino.note: North Kaibab Trail is open to foot traffic through Phantom Ranch, with stock use suspended. The National Park Service advises increased caution near Supai Tunnel and the lower trail due to Dragon Bravo Fire burn-scar hazards, including debris flows, rockfalls, and flash flooding with little to no warning even when storms are not visible overhead. The Flood Watch that was active August 14, 11am to 8pm MST, for this area has expired, and no new flood watch was active as of the August 16, 2026 check; the underlying burn-scar flash flood risk persists through the monsoon season regardless. Water is off at the North Kaibab Trailhead and Supai Tunnel, but on at Cottonwood Campground and Manzanita Day Use Area; single bottles and gallon jugs can be purchased at the North Rim General Store from 9am to 4pm daily. A section between Redwall Bridge and Cottonwood Campground is scheduled to close October 16, 2026 for waterline repair, not yet in effect. Grand Canyon National Park rates heat risk at Phantom Ranch as Major (last updated August 12, 2026). No Extreme Heat Warning was active for the Grand Canyon area below 4000 feet as of the same check. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park; National Weather Service Flagstaff.
